content: Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels of ponatinib by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may lead to reduced efficacy of ponatinib. It is recommended to avoid coadministration unless the benefits outweigh the risks. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for signs of reduced therapeutic effect. Rifampin decreases the levels of ponesimod by inducing CYP3A4 and UGT1A1 enzymes, potentially reducing its systemic exposure. Due to limited data, the clinical relevance of this interaction is unclear. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor closely for reduced efficacy. Rifampin reduces posaconazole levels by increasing its metabolism via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Conversely, posaconazole may slightly decrease rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug, and monitor closely if coadministration is necessary. Rifampin decreases pralsetinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration cannot be avoided, double the pralsetinib dose starting on day 7 of coadministration with rifampin. After discontinuing rifampin for at least 14 days, resume the previous pralsetinib dose. Monitor closely for therapeutic efficacy. Rifampin increases pravastatin toxicity through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may elevate the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects during coadministration. Rifampin reduces praziquantel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated, and coadministration should be avoided. Rifampin decreases prednisolone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor closely for reduced efficacy. Rifampin increases pretomanid levels, potentially leading to toxicity, while also reducing pretomanid levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Pretomanid regimens are associated with hepatotoxicity; avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents during treatment. Rifampin reduces primaquine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely for therapeutic efficacy if coadministration is necessary. Rifampin decreases primidone levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for therapeutic efficacy. Probenecid increases rifampin levels through an unspecified mechanism, potentially increasing the risk of toxicity. Use caution and monitor for adverse reactions during coadministration. Rifampin reduces progesterone levels (including intravaginal gel, micronized, and natural forms) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Nonhormonal contraceptives are advised. Rifampin decreases propafenone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for therapeutic efficacy. Rifampin reduces propofol levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely if coadministration is necessary. Rifampin decreases propranolol levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for therapeutic efficacy. Rifampin and pyrazinamide coadministration increases the risk of additive hepatotoxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces quazepam levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases quetiapine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces quinapril levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin decreases quinidine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely if coadministration is necessary. Rifampin reduces quinine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for therapeutic efficacy. Rifampin decreases quizartinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely for therapeutic efficacy. Rifampin reduces rabeprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin decreases raltegravir levels by increasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor closely for therapeutic efficacy. Rifampin reduces ramelteon levels by inducing CYP1A2, CYP3A4, and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin decreases ramipril levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin reduces ranolazine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely for therapeutic efficacy. Rifampin decreases rasagiline levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for therapeutic efficacy. Rifampin reduces regorafenib levels while increasing exposure to its active metabolite (M-5) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated, and coadministration should be avoided. Rifampin decreases repaglinide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces repotrectinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin increases resmetirom levels through mechanisms involving OATP1B1/3 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin increases revefenacin levels by inhibiting OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters, potentially increasing systemic exposure to its active metabolite. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases ribociclib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces rifabutin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated, and coadministration should be avoided. Rifampin reduces riluzole levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin decreases rimegepant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces riociguat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Data for dose adjustment are not available. Rifampin decreases ripretinib levels and its active metabolite (DP-5439) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces risperidone levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely for therapeutic efficacy. Rifampin decreases ritlecitinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases rivaroxaban levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inducers. Consider increasing the rivaroxaban dose if coadministration is necessary. Rifampin reduces roflumilast levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated, and coadministration should be avoided. Rifampin decreases rolapitant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces romidepsin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases ropinirole levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for therapeutic efficacy. Rifampin increases rosuvastatin toxicity through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may elevate the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects during coadministration. Rifampin reduces ruxolitinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for therapeutic efficacy. Rifampin increases sacubitril/valsartan levels through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely for adverse effects. Rifampin increases sarecycline levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrates. Rifampin decreases saxagliptin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for therapeutic efficacy. Rifampin reduces seladelpar levels by increasing its metabolism. Monitor biochemical response (e.g., ALP and bilirubin) when initiating rifampin during seladelpar treatment. Rifampin decreases selegiline levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for therapeutic efficacy. Rifampin reduces selexipag levels and its active metabolite by inducing CYP2C8, UGT1A3, and 2B7 enzymes. Increase the selexipag dose up to twice the typical dose if coadministered with rifampin. Rifampin decreases selpercatinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces selumetinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases sildenafil levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for therapeutic efficacy.
